newsitem.title: UK: British Borneo extends gain on bid talk.
newsitem.headline: British Borneo extends gain on bid talk.

text.p: Shares in British Borneo Plc rose on Wednesday, extending yesterday's advance amid bid speculation after the company's exploration deal in the Gulf of Mexico, dealers said.
The stock was up 60p at 912-1/2 by 0829 GMT in volume of 32,100 shares, after on Tuesday rising 50p.
The company said on Tuesday it had agreed to buy into a deep water oil prospect in the Gulf in a pact with BP Exploration and Oil Inc, part of British Petroleum Co Plc.
A report in the Financial Times said the company's increasing exposure to one of the world's most significant oil fields made it an attractive bid target.

Today's surge in British Borneo took the stock to a record high, some 40 percent above its level on December 17 -- the day before Gulf Canada ignited speculative interest in the sector with its bid for Clyde Petroleum Plc.
"It is an amazing move," said one market-maker in the stock. "Three days ago it was below 800p."
Analysts said the company's presence in the Gulf of Mexico was promising but warned that the stock was looking overheated after its recent sharp rise.

"It has got production coming through from the UK and has exploration upside," said Jurjen Lunshoff, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, "but at over 900p a share it looks to me as if it is beginning to have a hefty premium."
Lunshoff said Enterprise Oil Plc was one oil company that could wish to expand its presence in the Gulf, though recent gains in the stock had made it expensive for any potential bidder.
Enterprise shares were down 2-1/2p at 636-1/2 by 1018 GMT in active trade of 2.1 million shares while British Borneo was up 75p at 927-1/2, after earlier hitting a peak of 935p.

"The Gulf is very much a desirable exploration address offering great opportunity," said Lunshoff, "and yesterday's deal has been well received by the market in terms of the strategic objectives of the company."
